chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah Al-Jamurani Al-Razi, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Karim, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Jabir Al-Ju'fi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in a long hadith: And when you return from the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), a caller will call out to you. If you heard his statement, you would spend your life at the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And he will say: 'Bliss be to you, O servant of Allah! You have won and you are safe. Your past sins have been forgiven, so resume your deeds.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.

key_terms.طُوبَى: Bliss or happiness in the afterlife
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a visitor's sins when they return from the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this profound narration where a divine caller announces to the visitor of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) that their past sins are forgiven, urging them to 'resume the work' (ista'ni al-'amal). This highlights the Shia theological view of Ziyarah not merely as a ritual visit but as a transformative spiritual event that resets one's spiritual ledger, linking the intercessory status of the Ahl al-Bayt with immediate divine mercy.
